title: Kindle shows the bead being worked on: reader, epic graph, usage tab
description:
## What

The Kindle shows the bead being worked on. When a bead anywhere under ~/Projects moves to
in_progress, the dashboard jumps to a Bead tab: the bead's title, metadata and description,
read page by page. When that bead closes, the dashboard switches to a Graph tab showing the
bead's epic. Claude Code usage moves to its own Usage tab.

## Diagnosis (cm-dr0)

Weakest part: `crates/usage/src/message.rs` accepts exactly one message (a usage record), and
`app::Mode { Dashboard, Menu }` braids which page is shown with whether the menu is open.
Unresolved force: bead state lives in ~45 separate `.beads/` workspaces on the PC; br has no
hooks by design ("no daemons, no hooks", beads_rust README). Smallest move: a PC watcher pushes
a bead snapshot over the existing `ssh kindle usage ...` channel; the Kindle gains a push kind
and a view dimension, and renders on the device.

## Evidence

- br records `status_changed open->in_progress` and `assignee_changed` events (measured with br
  0.7.0 in a scratch workspace). br 0.7.6 is installed; `br audit log --since` spans issues.
- A read-only `br list` raises only CLOSE_WRITE on `beads.db*`; a real `br update` raises MODIFY
  on `beads.db`/`-wal` and MOVED_TO `issues.jsonl` (inotifywait, scratch workspace). A watcher
  that wakes on CLOSE_WRITE retriggers itself.
- On the Kindle (armv7, 1 GHz): franken_markdown parses a 5.2 KB bead description in 1.7 ms;
  frankenmermaid parses a 76-node/151-edge DOT graph in 15 ms and lays it out in 130 ms, 6 MB
  peak RSS; the static probe binary is 3.1 MB. Both libraries cross-build to
  armv7-unknown-linux-musleabi unchanged.
- The whole-project graph lays out 29744x1026: an unscoped graph is unreadable on 1024x758.
- Layouts were prototyped with the real eink canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/5Rik5JZ4sV2HEZUCrz2vmp

## Operator decision

2026-10-26, the operator's words verbatim:

- "pull the source and figure out how to have a hook that would give me a change of bead state,
  I want to show issue in progress on eink when I start working on a bead."
- Mechanism: "let's go with external watcher that would monitor beads in all of my projects, and
  would work to notify ~/Projects/mine/kindle whenever bead is being worked on, so that kindle
  can display information about active bead."
- Workspaces: "All under ~/Projects" (the option as offered: everything except test fixtures,
  paths containing /tests/ or temp_test; includes explore/ and the beads_rust clone).
- Several beads in progress: "Only the newest".
- Fields: "description and metadata".
- "Focus page looks good but design is not yet fixed. Let's make sure I can scroll the issue
  description. I want to be able to use reader style scrolling and have a scroll bar visible
  when text does not fit the page. And I would later want to have more inforation displayed,
  such as dependency graph, next beads graph to work on, and project metrics."
- "old session of mine, you are in charge. Tap zones a good. Dtop the footer move usage to usage
  tab. Yes to jump. When the bead closes switch to dependency graph tab. Use
  https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_markdown for markdown rendering and
  https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenmermaid for diagram engine (clone both projects,
  they have issues we might have to fix as we discover them)."
- Graph scope: "The bead's epic" (as offered: parent epic and all its children with their
  blocking edges; closed beads gray, active one inverted, ready ones bold).
- Dependencies: "Your forks" (as offered: fork both under the operator's GitHub account and pin
  kindle to the fork revs; fixes land in the forks first). Forks: igouss/franken_markdown,
  igouss/frankenmermaid.

This approves: the focus-page reader with tap zones (left third back, right two thirds
forward), a scroll bar only when the text overflows; no footer on the Bead tab; the usage
dashboard moved to a Usage tab (and so a regenerated golden page for that intended layout);
jumping to the Bead tab on a new active bead; switching to the Graph tab on close; the epic as
graph scope; franken_markdown and frankenmermaid as dependencies pinned to the forks, with fixes
made in the forks; the watcher over all workspaces under ~/Projects except test fixtures; the
newest in-progress bead only; the taking over of the old session's uncommitted message.rs work.

Later the same day, asked whether test setup may follow type changes, the operator answered:
"This is a green field project, you are in charge. You have my permission todo whatever you
need."

This approves, within this epic and the kindle repo: test edits, golden regenerations, gate,
guard and lint changes, refactoring scope, and design choices the epic needs. Each such change
is named in its commit message with its reason, never silent. Next and Metrics views stay
"later": not in this epic. Changes to the operator's other projects (the libraries' upstreams,
other repos under ~/Projects) are not covered: fixes to franken_markdown and frankenmermaid go
to the igouss forks as decided above.

title: message: a push names its kind; usage is the first
description: A push to the Kindle's socket carries a kind tag, so a second kind (the bead snapshot) can join without a second socket or command. Usage is the only kind in this step. Takes over the uncommitted message.rs/main.rs/serve.rs work from the operator's old session.
acceptance_criteria: A push without a kind or with an unknown kind is refused with a 'push:' error; a usage push round-trips; all gates green (cargo test, clippy, fmt).
close_reason: Committed a300fb0: tagged push kinds; tests 37+11+75 pass, clippy clean, armv7 build ok, cargo mutants 9 caught / 7 unviable on message.rs+main.rs

title: app: the menu is an overlay, not a mode; which page is shown is its own dimension
description: Mode{Dashboard,Menu} braids which page is shown with whether the menu is open: with a second page, Mode::Menu would have to remember the page beneath it. Split it: the menu is open or closed over whatever page is shown. Pure refactor: no visible change, goldens unchanged. The tab strip and the View sum type arrive with the second page (kindle-bxx.4); a one-tab strip or one-variant View rules nothing out (cm-jiu).
acceptance_criteria: Same goldens, same behaviour; menu tests pass with the new state; no wildcard arm; cargo mutants on app.rs kills every viable mutant; all gates green.
close_reason: Mode{Dashboard,Menu} renamed Menu{Closed,Open}: the type was only ever about the menu. Pure rename; test setup follows the rename, no assertion changed; goldens unchanged; gates green.

title: reader: the Bead view reads the description page by page
description: The Bead view lays the bead's title, metadata and markdown description (parsed by franken_markdown, pinned to the igouss fork) into lines with Liberation Sans, and splits them into pages: no line split across pages, no heading alone at the foot of a page. Tap the left third to go back a page, the right two thirds to go forward. A scroll bar shows only when the text runs past one page; its thumb is the share of the text on screen; the page shows 'n of m'. No footer. Page turns refresh quietly; a full flash every few turns. Pagination is a pure function, tested off the device.
acceptance_criteria: Zero, one and many pages tested (cm-srn); tap zones tested at their edges; golden pages for page 1 and a middle page of a real multi-page description; cargo mutants on the changed code kills every viable mutant; all gates green.
close_reason: Paged reader on the Bead tab: franken_markdown (igouss fork 4b705d1) AST -> styled, glued words -> lines -> pages (pure). Tap zones left third back / rest forward, flash every 6th turn, scroll bar + 'n of m' when >1 page. 149 usage tests; cargo mutants on the diff: 243 caught, 2 equivalent removed as dead code, 0 missed, 2 timeouts (infinite-loop mutants). Verified on the Kindle: 6-page real bead renders; injected taps turn exactly one page each.

title: bead push: the Kindle learns the active bead; a Bead tab beside Usage
description: A 'bead' push kind carries the newest in-progress bead (project, id, title, priority, type, assignee, when it went in progress, markdown description) or none. The header becomes a tab strip (Bead, Usage) with the menu button; the usage dashboard is the Usage tab. A new active bead jumps to the Bead tab at page 1 and closes the menu; the same bead re-pushed keeps its page; none shows 'nothing in progress'. The reading position belongs to the bead, so leaving the tab and coming back keeps it. Elapsed time runs on from the pushed clock. The Bead tab shows title and metadata; the paged description is kindle-bxx.3. Epic data and the switch to Graph on close are kindle-bxx.5.
acceptance_criteria: State-machine tests: first bead, same bead re-pushed, a different bead, bead closed, none ever, tab taps; a bad snapshot is refused; goldens regenerated for the tab header and shown to the operator; cargo mutants kills every viable mutant on changed code; all gates green.
close_reason: Bead push kind, Work state machine (Unknown/Idle/Active with page), View{Bead,Usage} with a header tab strip; usage moved to its tab. 97 usage tests + 43 eink; cargo mutants on the diff: 83 caught, 0 missed, 24 unviable; goldens full/menu regenerated for the tab header, bead/idle/waiting added.

title: graph: the Graph view draws the bead's epic with frankenmermaid
description: The bead push also carries the active bead's epic: each child's id, short title and status, and the blocking edges among them. A Graph tab renders it with frankenmermaid (pinned to the igouss fork) onto the e-ink canvas in grays: closed beads gray, the active bead inverted, ready beads bold. Labels are short (id and a few words). A graph larger than the page stays readable (scaled or paged with the tap zones). When the active bead closes, the Kindle switches to the Graph tab. Fixes needed in frankenmermaid go to the fork as their own commits.
acceptance_criteria: Golden page for a real epic (e.g. omarchy-expose-g3o); render time on the Kindle measured and stated; zero-, one- and many-node epics tested; all gates green.

title: watcher: the PC pushes the active bead when bead state changes
description: A host program watches every .beads/ workspace under ~/Projects except test fixtures (paths containing /tests/ or temp_test), picking up new workspaces. It wakes only on MODIFY or MOVED_TO (never CLOSE_WRITE, which its own reads cause), debounces, queries each workspace read-only (br list --status in_progress with --no-auto-flush --no-auto-import --allow-stale), takes the newest in-progress bead by its status_changed event, and pushes the bead snapshot over ssh only when it changed. An unreachable Kindle is logged and retried on the next change, never a crash. Runs as a systemd user service.
acceptance_criteria: Seen red first, then green, in a scratch workspace: no bead -> no push; in_progress -> push; close -> push of none; its own queries cause no push (no feedback loop); an end-to-end run on the real Kindle; README documents it.
close_reason: kindle-watch: inotify (MODIFY|MOVED_TO only) on every .beads workspace under ~/Projects except /tests/ and temp_test; read-only br queries; newest in-progress bead by its status_changed event; pushes on change and every 5 min heartbeat; unreachable Kindle logged and retried. host/check-watch.sh seen red (CLOSE_WRITE watched: queries 9->15 while idle) then green; 16 watcher tests + wire contract test on both sides; cargo mutants 25 caught 0 missed. Running as systemd user service; pushed kindle-bxx.6 live.

title: Use more of the franken libraries: diagrams in beads, partial refresh, better typesetting, Next/Metrics groundwork
description:
## What

Make better use of franken_markdown and frankenmermaid (both pinned to the igouss forks) on the
Kindle dashboard: richer reading on the Bead tab, cheaper refreshes, and the groundwork for the
Next and Metrics views the operator asked for "later" in kindle-bxx.

## Context

Proposed after kindle-bxx, from a survey of both libraries. Only these parts have been used and
verified on the device: franken_markdown's parser (`franken_markdown::parse` -> `ast::Document`)
and frankenmermaid's parse -> layout -> canvas path (`fm_parser::parse`,
`fm_render_canvas::render_to_canvas` through `Canvas2dContext`, implemented in
`crates/usage/src/graph/paint.rs`). Every other capability named in the child beads was seen in
source or module docs only and is marked "unverified": the first step of each is to confirm it.

Fixes the libraries need go to the igouss forks as their own commits (operator decision in
kindle-bxx), and kindle moves its pinned rev.

## Operator decision

2026-10-26, the operator's words verbatim: "file beads for 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9" (items of a ranked
list of library capabilities to use next).

This approves filing these beads. None: every policy question goes back to the operator,
including whether and in what order to implement them.

title: reader: mermaid diagrams in a bead's description are drawn, not shown as code
description: A fenced ```mermaid block in a bead description is drawn inline on the Bead tab as a diagram, with the same frankenmermaid renderer and gray styling the Graph tab uses, sized to the text column and kept on one page (a diagram taller than a page gets a page of its own). Other fenced blocks stay code. franken_markdown also has its own diagram compiler (diagrams.rs, unverified): pick one renderer and say why.
acceptance_criteria: Goldens: a description with a flowchart and one with a sequence diagram; a diagram the parser rejects falls back to showing its source as code; pagination never splits a diagram; mutants clean on changed code; verified on the Kindle.

title: screen: a change refreshes only the part of the panel it touched
description: Today every change redraws and refreshes the whole panel. Refresh only the region that changed: a sibling bead's status on the Graph tab, the elapsed time in the header, a page turn. frankenmermaid's layout reports dirty_regions for incremental layout (unverified); the Kindle panel accepts an update rectangle (MXCFB_SEND_UPDATE takes one). Full flashes against ghosting keep their schedule.
acceptance_criteria: On the device: a status change on the Graph tab updates only that node's rectangle (measured from the update region sent); a header tick updates only the header; a full refresh still happens on the existing schedule; mutants clean on changed code.

title: reader: paragraphs are broken as a whole and pages are chosen to avoid bad breaks
description: Replace the reader's greedy line filling and greedy pagination with franken_markdown's TeX-style paragraph breaker (layout.rs, metrics pluggable through its AdvanceMetrics trait, unverified) and its optimal pagination (pagination.rs, bounded shortest-path search, unverified), measured with the panel's Liberation Sans. Keep the reader's invariants: no line split across pages, no heading ending a page, layout a pure function of the bead.
acceptance_criteria: On the real g3o.13 description: fewer very short or very loose lines than today (stated as a measured count before/after); existing reader invariants still tested; goldens regenerated and shown to the operator; mutants clean on changed code.

title: reader: tables are drawn as tables
description: Markdown tables in a bead description are drawn with aligned columns, a bold head row and rules, instead of today's 'a · b · c' lines. A table wider than the text column stays readable (wraps cells, or another rule the operator approves). franken_markdown has table layout code (code_table_flow, unverified).
acceptance_criteria: Goldens: a narrow table, a wide table, a one-column table; column alignment from the Markdown (:--, :-:, --:) honoured; pagination keeps a row whole; mutants clean on changed code.

title: reader: code blocks are syntax highlighted in grays
description: Fenced code with a language tag is highlighted for e-ink: keywords bold, comments and strings in grays, using franken_markdown's highlighter (highlight.rs and lang_* lexers, unverified). Untagged code and unknown languages render as today.
acceptance_criteria: Goldens: Rust, shell and an unknown language; contrast of every gray used is legible on the panel (checked on the device); mutants clean on changed code.

title: eink: text is kerned and uses ligatures
description: Text on the panel is set with the font's kerning pairs (and ligatures where Liberation Sans has them), using fmd-font's Kerning and Ligatures (unverified) or another source. Measurement and drawing must agree exactly, everywhere text is laid out (reader, usage page, graph labels), so that layout stays consistent with what is drawn.
acceptance_criteria: A test pair such as 'AV' or 'To' measures and draws narrower than unkerned; every golden is regenerated and shown to the operator; reader page counts change only where kerning moves a line break (listed); mutants clean on changed code.

title: graph: find out which diagram types the canvas renderer draws, for the Next and Metrics views
description: Spike. The operator wants a Next view (beads to work on next) and a Metrics view (project metrics). List which Mermaid diagram types frankenmermaid parses and which the canvas renderer actually draws through Canvas2dContext on the panel (detect_type and layout_algorithms_markdown() are a start, unverified). For each candidate type, render a sample with real bead data on the e-ink canvas and judge legibility.
acceptance_criteria: A short report in docs/ (or the bead's notes) with one rendered sample per usable type from real br data, which types fail and why, and a recommendation for Next and Metrics; no product code required; the operator decides the views.

title: graph: the critical path and next ready beads of an epic
description: Compute, for the active epic, what is ready now and the longest chain of open beads still to do (critical path), for use by a Next view and as emphasis on the Graph tab. fm-layout has an optional network-analysis feature (fnx-integration) and cycle clustering (unverified); the computation may equally be done directly on the epic's blocking edges. Cycles in br dependencies must not hang or crash it.
acceptance_criteria: Pure function with tests for zero, one and many beads, a cycle, a diamond, and a fully closed epic; on the real g3o epic the result is checked by hand; mutants clean on changed code.
